::: {.why}
The most heavily asked family in trading interviews because a random walk is the simplest model of a price, and the questions test whether you can set up a difference equation quickly.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Solve six random walk problems under a clock, setting up the recursion within the first minute.
- State the reflection principle and use it to get the distribution of the maximum.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [40 min]{.task-min} Forty minutes, six problems. For each, the setup is a difference equation with boundary conditions, and the discipline is to write it down before attempting to solve. Most failures here are setup failures rather than algebra failures.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Do the reflection principle properly once: every path that exceeds a level and ends below it maps to a path that ends above the reflected level, which gives the distribution of the maximum in one line. Then use it for the expected maximum over n steps and check numerically.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [Grinstead & Snell — Introduction to Probability (free PDF)](https://math.dartmouth.edu/~prob/prob/prob.pdf) [textbook]{.res-kind}
- [Jane Street — puzzle archive with solutions](https://www.janestreet.com/puzzles/archive/index.html) [problems]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A scored six-problem session, plus the reflection principle applied to the distribution of the maximum and checked numerically.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
A symmetric random walk starts at 0. Give the probability it reaches plus 10 before minus 5, and the expected time to stop.
:::
